issues.legal_issue: An insolvency court may determine whether a transfer made more than two years before insolvency proceedings was void from its inception as a sham or fictitious transaction.
material_facts: A debtor had executed a gift deed in favour of his wife several years before insolvency proceedings began.
The receiver challenged the deed as a sham and fictitious transaction under which no title had passed.

The insolvency court declared the deed void, but the High Court set aside that decision on the ground that the court lacked jurisdiction to examine a transfer made more than two years before the proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The insolvency court had jurisdiction under Section 4 of the Provincial Insolvency Act, 1920, to determine whether the transfer was sham and void from its inception; Section 53 did not bar that inquiry. The appeal was allowed and the matter remitted to the High Court for fresh disposal on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4 confers broad power to decide questions of title arising in insolvency, subject to the Act’s other provisions. Section 53 concerns transfers that are voidable, and its two-year limit does not exclude the court’s jurisdiction to determine whether an alleged sham or fictitious transfer was void from the outset, in which case no title passed and no annulment is necessary. The Court agreed with Padamsi Premchand v. Laxman Vishnu Despande and Madan Kumar v. M/s. Hari Narain Agrawal, and referred to the supporting approaches in Haji Anwar Khan v. Mohamad Khan, Radha Krishna Thakur v. Official Receiver, Biseswar Chaudhuri v. Kanhai Sing, G.N. Godbole v. Mt. Nani Bai, and Budha Mal v. Official Receiver; it declined to follow Amjad Ali v. Nand Lal Tandon.

rule.if: insolvency_proceeding and transfer_challenged_as_sham and transfer_alleged_void_from_inception and transfer_preceded_insolvency_by_more_than_two_years

predicates.insolvency_proceeding: A proceeding is brought to determine a debtor’s insolvency and administer the debtor’s property.
predicates.transfer_challenged_as_sham: A receiver or other person responsible for the insolvency estate challenges a purported transfer as sham or fictitious.
predicates.transfer_alleged_void_from_inception: The challenge alleges that the transaction was ineffective from the outset and passed no title.
predicates.transfer_preceded_insolvency_by_more_tha: The purported transfer occurred more than two years before the insolvency proceeding began.

issues.definition: When an insolvency proceeding involves a purported transfer made more than two years before it began that is challenged as sham and void from the outset, the insolvency court may determine whether the transfer was void.
